{{Quote|I'm a member of the Imperial Senate on a diplomatic mission to Alderaan!|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Princess Leia]]|<ref name="ANH" />}}
The '''Imperial Senate''' or '''Imperial Congress''' was the ''de jure'' legislative body of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], though in practice it held little real authority. Instead, it served mainly as an advisory body to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. The Imperial Senate was the successor to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]], which was reformed when the then [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine [[Declaration of a New Order|declared himself]] sole ruler.

==History==
===Rise of the Empire===
{{Dialogue|Amidala|Do you think he will dismantle the Senate?|Mothma|Why bother? As a practical matter, the Senate no longer exists.|Danu|The constitution is in shreds...amendment after amendment...|attr=Senators Padmé Amidala, Mon Mothma, and Giddean Danu discussing Palpatine's rise to power|src=<ref name="RotS" />}}

[[File:Sithdelscener1pic2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Bail Organa informs other senators that Palpatine has declared a new system of regional Governors]]
The Imperial Senate [[Declaration of a New Order|was established]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] after the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] was founded by the self-appointed [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], transforming the old [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. Rather than risk directly seizing power and overthrowing the Senate, Palpatine had subtly manipulated the Galactic Senate into voting incrementally more and more [[Emergency Powers Act/Legends|emergency powers]] to the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Chancellorship]] over the course of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. By [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|the end of the conflict]], Palpatine had gained near-dictatorial powers. The final stroke came following [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends#Duel on the Invisible Hand|the death]] of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] leader [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] during the closing days of the war, when Palpatine issued a [[Sector Governance Decree/Legends|decree]] creating a new class of [[Planetary Governor/Legends|Planetary Governors]] and [[Sector/Legends|Sector]] [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] appointed directly by the Chancellorship, to oversee all [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] in the Republic. A minority of [[Senator/Legends|Senators]] [[Delegation of 2000|protested this action]], but Palpatine brushed their complaints aside.

[[File:Declaration.png|thumb|left|300px|Palpatine declares the formation of the Galactic Empire to the now-Imperial Senate]]
Within a few days, the Clone Wars ended with the death of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] in a duel with [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and the execution of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] at the hands of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. With the justification of a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Showdown on Coruscant|rebellion]], Palpatine ordered [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Republic troops]] to [[Order 66/Legends|wipe out]] the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], and in a speech before the Senate, proclaimed himself Emperor. Senators who vocally resisted were intimidated into silence through brief imprisonment.

On the whole, however, the transition from Galactic Senate to Imperial Senate went quietly and without major incident. Emperor Palpatine did not want to risk tarnishing his public support by making a bold grab for truly absolute power, so he allowed the organization to continue to nominally exist, though it had been largely gutted of any meaningful power over the new Empire's functions. Under the advice of [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] shortly before her death, Senators [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Organa]] and [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], along with other Senators from the Delegation of 2000, did not directly confront Palpatine's declaration of a Galactic Empire. Realizing they had already lost, and that further resistance would only be seized upon by Palpatine as justification for dismantling what little remained of the Senate, they determined that their best remaining option was to bide their time in silence. In addition, the newly formed Empire had always intended for the Imperial Senate to simply be a transitional buffer between the Old Republic and the New Order.<ref name="Imperial Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

As the years passed, however, Palpatine gradually reshaped the Senate to better serve his regime. He quietly replaced many members of the original legislature with politicians more aligned with his New Order, often rewarding their loyalty by promoting them above their longer-serving colleagues. Over time, very little of the original Republican Senate remained, leaving behind a body that existed largely to legitimize the Emperor's will.<ref name="Rebellion Era Campaign Guide">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

After [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] openly spoke against the Emperor, around [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], the Senate sent Princess [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] to [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] as an observer of the [[slavery/Legends|enslavement]] of the native [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] species. In reality, the Emperor wanted to keep Leia in this dangerous environment, in the custody of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Ozzik Sturn]], to keep her father silent; in case Leia had to be eliminated, the planetary conflict would provide a convenient excuse. The Senate's plot failed when she was [[Mission to Kashyyyk (Great Jedi Purge)|rescued]] by [[Galen Marek]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Force Unleashed">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref><ref name="The Art and Making of Star Wars: The Force Unleashed">''[[The Art and Making of Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

Although at the time of the Empire's formation a majority of senators were loyal to Palpatine, the Imperial Senate was still a prime (if often clandestine) source of resistance to Palpatine's authority, and despite its changes, came to be known as the "last remnants of the Old Republic." Certain Senators&mdash;many of whom later joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]]&mdash;were known for using the Senate as a platform to voice proposals attempting to moderate Palpatine's rule, although always under the guise of perfect loyalty. A few Senator also proceeded to secretly give aid to the Rebel Alliance. However, those senators' actions did not go unnoticed by [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]].<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> Prior to its dissolution, the Imperial Senate, under the approval of the Emperor, also issued [[Intergalactic Passport]]s to anyone in the galaxy to give them expressed permission to travel through the six primary galaxies.<ref name="Intergalactic Passport real-life artifact">[[Intergalactic Passport (real-life artifact)|Intergalactic Passport]]</ref> Similarly, the Senate also had access to another version of the Intergalactic Passport that was issued by them directly via the [[President of the Imperial Senate]], although it had some restrictions: namely, it couldn't actually guarantee the owners' safety when traveling through any portions of Imperial Space that were under the direct control of the Emperor without either the Emperor's permission, or barring that, meeting with the commander of the Dantooine Base.<ref name="Star Wars Intergalactic Passport">''[[The Star Wars Intergalactic Passport]]''</ref>

===Dissolution===
{{Quote|The Imperial Senate will no longer be of any concern to us. I've just received word that the Emperor has dissolved the council permanently. The last remnants of the Old Republic have been swept away.|[[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]]|<ref name="ANH" />}}
[[File:EmperorPalpatineHologram.jpg|200px|thumb|Hologram of Emperor Palpatine, taken from the speech in which he announced the disbanding of the Senate]]
In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] (35:3:5), Palpatine ordered the Imperial Senate to be [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|shut down]] "for the duration of the emergency," ostensibly due to the widespread dissemination of the [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|Declaration of Rebellion]] over the previous months. In truth, the Declaration of Rebellion was merely an excuse to eliminate the Imperial Senate permanently, due to it being a remnant of the Old Republic as well as having Rebel sympathizers among the various senators, and furthermore its role as a transitional buffer had already been expended, with only officers in the Imperial Military being notified of this.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> As such, it was never revived. To fill the open void in the Imperial government, [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|COMPNOR's]] [[Select Committee/Legends|Select Committee]] stepped up to the task of overseeing the vast Imperial bureaucracy. The [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]] became the central leadership within the Empire, while the Moffs and [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moffs]] retained direct control over their territories.

Eventually, the Imperial legislature was handled by various councils, most composed of Moffs: the [[Central Committee of Grand Moffs]], the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]], and finally, the [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Council of Moffs]].

According to the [[Bureau of Operations/Legends|Bureau of Operations]] of [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]], the Rebel Alliance managed to rescue many former Senators who were willing to use their political influence to oppose the Empire. To prevent these politicians from openly supporting the Rebellion, Imperial Intelligence sent teams to attack the Senators' hideouts.<ref name="SWG:Dsh">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=terminal|Imperial|Destroy senators' hideout}}</ref>

[[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]] marked the year that the Imperial Senate was succeeded by the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]].

==Powers==
[[File:CorellianTreaty-TFUComic.jpg|thumb|right|240px|Discontented Imperial Senators form the Rebel Alliance]]
Past its name, the organization differed somewhat from its Republican forebear. Whereas the Galactic Senate had held both legislative and executive power, the Imperial Senate held only legislative power&mdash;though most of this power was in the hands of the Emperor, as he was the overall ultimate authority. Despite this, the Imperial Senate still held limited judicial authority, enough to try high ranking officials in the Empire and, possibly, handle cases tied into the [[Supreme Court/Legends|Supreme Court]]. The Emperor allowed the Senate to provide him counsel in enacting new laws. It also had nominal oversight of the Imperial bureaucracy and worked on the Imperial budget. However, the Emperor made it clear that his judgments would be final: his decrees would be issued without debates, court proceedings, or Senatorial overrides. The Emperor could also call and dismiss the Senate at will. The Senate could also pass amendments to the [[Imperial Charter/Legends|Imperial Charter]] and apparently had at least nominal oversight of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]].

The day-to-day head of the Senate was no longer the [[Vice Chair/Legends|Vice Chair]], but the [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]] as [[President of the Senate]]. The Senate was, at least in theory, responsible for choosing a new Emperor upon the death or abdication of the current holder of the throne. As Palpatine had no intention of ever dying or abdicating, however, this seemingly important power was little more than a formality. 

Despite these limitations, the Imperial Senate retained a measure of authority during the early years of the Empire. Many Senators still regarded themselves as vital participants in the machinery of governance. Dissenters continued to hope that the Senate might serve as a means to restore lost liberties or enact limited reforms. Although their influence over the Emperor was negligible, Senators continued to command respect among officials and across the galaxy.<ref name="TFU Campaign">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

The Senate also remained a platform for negotiation on regional and sector-level issues outside of direct Imperial control. As a public forum whose proceedings reached vast audiences, it allowed dissenting voices to circulate&mdash;even when the institution itself lacked the strength to oppose the Emperor's will directly.<ref name="TFU Campaign" />

==Composition==
The Imperial Senate was made up of groups of [[Congressman|congressmen]]: Senators and [[Junior Representative/Legends|representatives]], representing sectors in the Empire. Some were elected directly, while others were appointed by a planet's ruler.

Because of "[[High Human Culture/Legends|Human High Culture]]," most of the [[Alien/Legends|alien]] Senators were replaced by [[Human/Legends|Humans]], who ended up representing worlds that were entirely [[Non-huMan|non-human]], though alien senators were not unheard of, especially in the early days of the Empire. In addition, most power was transferred to the Core Worlds. The reason for this human majority, as well as the Core-centric political rule, was justified in the official field manual for the Imperial Military, which claimed that the alien species of the Rim were unpredictable and predisposed to violent outbursts, citing the Republic Senate's history as proof.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

Committees and Subcommittees included:
*[[Delegation of 2000]]
*[[Senate Budgetary Committee/Legends|Senate Budgetary Committee]]
*[[Imperial Military Oversight Commission]]
*[[Finance Committee/Legends|Finance Committee]]

==Behind the scenes==
Palpatine's transformation of the Galactic Senate into the Imperial Senate mirrors how the Roman Republic was transformed into the Roman Empire by its first emperor, Augustus. Rather than risk further confrontation with the Roman Republic's Senate, Augustus allowed the Senators to continue meeting, but they had been stripped of any real executive power, continuing as little more than an advisory council which he could simply ignore at his leisure. The only difference being that unlike Palpatine, Augustus never dissolved the Senate in his lifetime.
